title: Singtel mobile network disruptions on 16–18 March 2026
asked: MPs asked about the causes and impact of Singtel's mobile network disruptions on 16–18 March 2026, how many users were affected, whether emergency or essential services were affected, and what IMDA will do to strengthen network resilience, failover systems, redundancy and consumer safeguards.
asked_by: Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye, Dr Neo Kok Beng and Ms Poh Li San
response: Mrs Josephine Teo said Singtel had mobile service difficulties from 16 to 18 March 2026. The 16 March incident affected more than 600,000 customers, lasted about nine hours and was attributed to a mechanical fault; a 17 March incident affected about 2,000 customers and was attributed to a software bug; and 18 March issues were resolved within an hour. IMDA is investigating, found no evidence of cyberattacks so far, and is checking whether emergency calls were affected. She said IMDA is reviewing telecom resilience regulations, requires one-hour incident resolution, audits, >99% outdoor coverage and failover systems, and will publish findings and take strong action if lapses are found.

key_points.point: Singtel had mobile service difficulties from 16 to 18 March 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: between 16 and 18 March 2026, Singtel experienced difficulties with its mobile service network.

key_points.point: The 16 March incident affected more than 600,000 Singtel mobile customers.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: an incident on 16 March affected more than 600,000 Singtel mobile customers.

key_points.point: The disruption lasted about nine hours.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: the disruption lasted for about nine hours.

key_points.point: The cause was attributed to a mechanical fault at one of Singtel's network facilities.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: The cause of the incident was attributed to a mechanical fault at one of Singtel’s network facilities.

key_points.point: A separate 17 March incident affected about 2,000 customers and was attributed to a software bug from a planned IT system update.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: A separate incident reported on 17 March affected about 2,000 Singtel mobile customers and was attributed to a software bug from a planned IT system update.

key_points.point: On 18 March, some customers had intermittent connectivity issues during peak network traffic in the late afternoon.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: On 18 March, some Singtel mobile customers experienced intermittent connectivity issues during peak network traffic in the late afternoon.

key_points.point: IMDA is investigating and there is no evidence so far that the incidents were due to cyberattacks.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: Thus far, there is no evidence that the incidents were due to cyberattacks.

key_points.point: IMDA is investigating whether emergency service calls were affected, with no such reports so far.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: IMDA is also investigating whether calls to emergency services were affected by the incidents, even though there are no such reports thus far.

key_points.point: Service providers must resolve service incidents within one hour, or IMDA may take enforcement action and impose financial penalties.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: service providers are required to ensure that service incidents are resolved within one hour, failing which IMDA may take enforcement actions and impose financial penalties.

key_points.point: Providers must ensure more than 99% nationwide outdoor mobile service coverage at all times.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: ensuring more than 99% nation-wide outdoor mobile service coverage at all times.

key_points.point: IMDA requires key providers to have redundancies and failover systems for core network functions.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: This includes providing redundancies and failover systems for core network functions.

key_points.point: IMDA is reviewing telecom service resilience regulations.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: IMDA is reviewing telecom service resilience regulations to ensure they remain effective.

key_points.point: Singtel has provided one-time rebates for affected mobile subscribers.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: Singtel has provided one-time rebates for affected mobile subscribers as part of their service recovery.

key_points.point: IMDA will publish findings after investigations and take strong regulatory action if lapses are identified.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: It will publish its findings after investigations are completed and will not hesitate to take strong regulatory action should any lapses be identified.

key_points.point: Stress testing has to take place, and investigations may show where it needs to be improved.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: The stress testing obviously has to take place

key_points.point: Average telecom incidents came down to six per year in 2021–2025.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: that has come down to an average of six incidents per year.

key_points.point: Average incident duration fell from eight hours to six-and-a-half hours.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: The average duration of the incidents has also come down from eight hours to six-and-a-half hours.

key_points.point: Compensation was done on Singtel's own volition.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: this was done on Singtel's own volition.

key_points.point: Mobile switching would not respond to all kinds of service disruptions.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: It would not be able to respond to all kinds of service disruptions.

key_points.point: Service providers can improve the timeliness of updates to subscribers and the public.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: service providers can certainly improve the timeliness of their updates to their subscribers as well as to members of the public.

key_points.point: The UK and Germany have limited compensation arrangements, such as for broadband or landline loss only.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: the scope is quite limited, such as for loss of service for broadband or landline only

key_points.point: IMDA and CSA will look seriously into state-sponsored cyber threat issues.
key_points.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
key_points.quote: IMDA, together with CSA, will have to look very seriously into these issues.

left_open: Specific lessons learnt from the incidents, pending the completion of IMDA's investigations.
Whether IMDA and CSA conducted independent cybersecurity investigations beyond Singtel's internal investigations and whether they uncovered anything new.
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on causes, compensation, stress testing, cross-telco switching, real-time outage updates and cybersecurity investigations.
